The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. Together these three laws constitute a formal foundation for SToE and generate specific, testable consequences for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and the foundations of mathematics.

First introduced in Voronin (2021) and developed across subsequent work, these laws are here stated explicitly and systematically for the first time. The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Connection holds that connections between information points are created exclusively by observers or creators. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. Together these three laws constitute a formal foundation for SToE and generate specific, testable consequences for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and the foundations of mathematics.

The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Connection holds that connections between information points are created exclusively by observers or creators. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. Together these three laws constitute a formal foundation for SToE and generate specific, testable consequences for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and the foundations of mathematics.

The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. First introduced in Voronin (2021) and developed across subsequent work, these laws are here stated explicitly and systematically for the first time. The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Connection holds that connections between information points are created exclusively by observers or creators. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. Together these three laws constitute a formal foundation for SToE and generate specific, testable consequences for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and the foundations of mathematics.

First introduced in Voronin (2021) and developed across subsequent work, these laws are here stated explicitly and systematically for the first time. The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Connection holds that connections between information points are created exclusively by observers or creators. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. Description: Current artificial intelligence systems exhibit characteristic failure modes: context-bounded memory loss, inability to navigate previously failed reasoning paths, and the absence of genuine structural self-evaluation. This paper argues that these failures are not incidental engineering limitations but consequences of a fundamental architectural gap: current AI systems are built without reference to the foundational laws governing information. Drawing on the three foundational laws of the Special Theory of Everything (SToE) — the Law of Information Conservation, the Law of Connection, and the Law of Autoinjection — we derive the specific architectural requirements that a genuinely information-native AI system must satisfy. We describe the required vessel: a persistent reasoning graph in which no information point is discarded, a topology-aware navigation mechanism distinct from similarity-based retrieval, and a structural self-evaluation loop grounded in autoinjection.

Description: This paper presents the three foundational laws of the Special Theory of Everything (SToE): the Law of Information Conservation, the Law of Connection, and the Law of Autoinjection. First introduced in Voronin (2021) and developed across subsequent work, these laws are here stated explicitly and systematically for the first time. The Law of Information Conservation holds that no information point vanishes from reality — it can only lose connections with other information points. The Law of Connection holds that connections between information points are created exclusively by observers or creators. The Law of Autoinjection holds that everything, including the information field itself, is an information point, with no exterior to the system. Together these three laws constitute a formal foundation for SToE and generate specific, testable consequences for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and the foundations of mathematics.
